newsitem.title: USA: J&L prices rise in Q2, remain below 1996.
newsitem.headline: J&L prices rise in Q2, remain below 1996.

text.p: J&L Specialty Steel Inc said Monday that shipments continued to top the year-ago pace in the second quarter, while prices rose 5.6 percent from the first quarter but remained below those of a year earlier.
Second quarter shipments totalled 85,938 tons, up 12.3 percent from 76,540 tons a year earlier.
Shipments for the first six months of 1997 were 178,699 tons, compared with 159,973 tons in the first half of 1996, an increase of 11.7 percent.
"We are pleased with the improvement in our year-to-date shipments as well as the 5.6 percent increase in average selling prices from the first quarter of 1997," Chief Executive Claude Kronk said.

"However, even with this increase, the average selling price for the current quarter was 12.2 percent lower than in the second quarter of 1996, as the domestic marketplace continues to be very competitive due to the high levels of imported stainless steel sheet," he said.
The company reported a second quarter loss of $3.4 million on net sales of $161.3 million, compared with net income of $7.8 million on net sales of $163.7 million a year earlier.
Pre-operating costs for the company's Direct Roll Anneal and Pickle (DRAP) Line at its Midland, Pa., plant reduced second quarter net income by $0.11 per share, it said.
"All individual components of the DRAP Line have been tested, and commissioning of the line continues to move forward," Kronk said.

"Earlier this month, our very first attempt to produce hot rolled annealed and pickled product was successful. As the commissioning process continues, our efforts are now focused on coordinating those additional components needed to produce cold rolled products, while we continue to routinely produce additional hot rolled annealed and pickled material.
"Our commissioning progress is generally within our overall targeted time frame, and we are still confident that we will be able to ramp up to normal production levels during the fourth quarter."
